paras: **1-month view.** These calls change every two weeks on average and showed no forward value in the backtest. Use the 3-month view for decisions.
**Value** fits the 1-month checklist best: 8 of 14 signals confirm and 6 contradict. Next is Risk ON: 6 of 15 confirm and 6 contradict, so Value is ahead by 0.14 on score.
It took the lead this week (so far); last week the best fit was Growth.
For Value, strongest confirmations: Low P/E +8.3%, R. Yields −27bp and XLB + XLF / SPY +5.5%. Pushing against it: Long + Med. Gov. bonds +3.3% and EM / DM −7.0%.

Your chart's playbook for Value: favors Small / Large cap, XLB + XLF / SPY, Low P/E, Cyclicals / non-cyclicals, Highβ / Lowβ, Oil, Commodities and EM / DM; expects weakness in Long + Med. Gov. bonds, Corporate bonds and Gold.

Rates backdrop, context only: over 3 months the curve made a **bear flattener** (+48bp on the 2-year, +32bp on the 10-year) with the S&P 5.3% above its 200-day average. Since 1990, that combination was followed by +6.9% a year for the S&P over the next 3 months, against +11.2% on average.
backdrop: **Fed:** funds rate 3.88%. The 2-year at 4.70% sits 82bp above fed funds, so the market expects hikes.
**Inflation:** Core PCE 3.1% y/y (2.9% annualized over 3 months) vs the 2% target, steady.
**Labor:** unemployment 4.2%, initial claims 197k (4-week avg), Sahm rule calm at 0.00.

curve_table.name: Bull steepener
curve_table.note: Short rates falling fastest, so the market expects Fed cuts. Your chart calls this Risk ON, but stocks fell on average while it happened, and what came next depended on whether growth was holding up.

curve_table.note: Long yields falling fastest. Matches the chart's Growth playbook, and the best stretch for stocks afterwards.
